title: PTNK 2025 · Tiếng Anh Không chuyên
subtitle: Đề thi tuyển sinh lớp 10 · Trường Phổ thông Năng khiếu · 2025-2026

questions.q: Choose the word whose underlined part pronounces differently from the other three.
questions.explanation: "lived" ends in the voiced /v/, so -ed is /d/; after the voiceless /p/, /k/ and /f/ of skipped, ticked and laughed it is /t/.

questions.q: Choose the word whose underlined part pronounces differently from the other three.
questions.explanation: "through" is /θruː/ with the /uː/ sound; although, thorough and borrow all end in the /əʊ/ (or unstressed /ə/–/oʊ/) vowel.

questions.q: Choose the word whose primary stress position differs from the other three.
questions.explanation: vo-lun-TEER is stressed on the third syllable; di-SAS-ter, im-POR-tant and e-LEC-tric on the second.

questions.q: Choose the word whose primary stress position differs from the other three.
questions.explanation: dis-be-LIEF is stressed on the last syllable; MA-ni-fest, THE-o-ry and KI-lo-gram on the first.

questions.q:
Tam: 'Hey Huy! I just came back from the Philippines. We were on vacation.'
Huy: '______'
questions.explanation: Tam has just returned from a trip, so the natural reply is to ask to hear about it; "Have a wonderful trip" is said before a trip and "Glad you enjoyed it" needs Tam to have said she enjoyed it.

questions.q: _____ every student in my university class is Vietnamese, but there are also a few students from Laos.
questions.explanation: "Almost every student" — "almost" modifies "every"; "most of" would need "the students", not "every student".

questions.q: Because the show _____ at 4:30 p.m, we have about one hour to get to the theater.
questions.explanation: A fixed timetable or scheduled event (a show at 4:30) takes the present simple, and time clauses with "because" of a schedule do not use "will".

questions.q: The police is talking to my neighbors, none of _____ could give them any useful information.
questions.explanation: After a preposition ("none of") the relative pronoun for people must be the object form "whom".

questions.q: It's a good sign that your daughter _____ her friends at the new school.
questions.explanation: "get on with somebody" = have a friendly relationship with; that is the "good sign" at a new school.

questions.q: He can't legally drive without a valid driving _____.
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is "driving license" (the official document allowing you to drive).

questions.q: A friend of _____ asked to share my apartment, but I don't think we are close enough to do that.
questions.explanation: The double-possessive pattern is "a friend of mine" — "of" + possessive pronoun.

questions.q: Mr. White _____ something in the kitchen because it smells great.
questions.explanation: "must be + V-ing" expresses a confident deduction about something happening right now — the smell is the evidence.

questions.q: Marie Curie is one of _____ female scientists who have won the Nobel Prize in science.
questions.explanation: "one of the few + plural noun + who…" refers to a specific small group defined by the relative clause, so the definite article is needed.

questions.q: My grandfather forgets _____ to Tasmania in his youth. He has no memory of it!
questions.explanation: "forget + V-ing" refers to a past experience one no longer remembers, and "have been to a place" = have visited it, so the perfect gerund "having been" is required.

questions.q: Some students often learn long definitions by _____ without truly understanding what they mean.
questions.explanation: "learn by rote" = memorise through repetition without understanding — exactly what "without truly understanding what they mean" describes.

questions.q: His family wanted (A) to know where (B) was he last night (C) when they could not reach him (D) by phone.
questions.explanation: In an indirect question the word order is subject + verb: "where he was last night", not "where was he".

questions.q: Molly speaks (A) so good Mandarin (B) that some people (C) have mistaken her (D) for a native speaker.
questions.explanation: Before an adjective + noun ("good Mandarin") the pattern is "such … that", not "so … that": "speaks such good Mandarin that…".

questions.q: If Arthur (A) had arrived (B) at the theater sooner, he (C) would catch his girlfriend (D) flirting with her fellow cast members.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: "If + past perfect, would have + past participle" — "he would have caught his girlfriend".

questions.q: The man admitted to (A) steal the luxurious watch, (B) but he denied (C) knowing anything (D) related to the kidnapping.
questions.explanation: "admit (to) + V-ing": "admitted to stealing the luxurious watch".

questions.q: Aurora borealis, or the Northern Lights, (A) is a beautiful natural phenomenon (B) occurring in some Northern countries, (C) that many people want to experience at least once in (D) their lifetime.
questions.explanation: A non-defining relative clause after a comma cannot use "that"; it must be "which many people want to experience".

questions.passage:
1. The entire population of Gaza is facing acute food insecurity, with nearly half a million people now suffering catastrophic hunger, according to a new report from the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC). Since all humanitarian aid was blocked on 2 March, malnutrition and hunger have worsened dramatically. The IPC estimates that 71,000 children and over 17,000 mothers urgently need treatment for acute malnutrition, a sharp rise from earlier in the year. Without immediate intervention, food insecurity, malnutrition, and mortality levels are expected to exceed famine thresholds in the coming months.

2. The crisis is being fueled by ongoing conflict, a complete blockade, and the total closure of border crossings, which have now been shut for over two months, the longest in Gaza's history. Food prices in local markets have soared to unaffordable levels, leaving even basic items out of reach for most families. Despite this, more than 116,000 metric tons of food aid, enough to feed one million people for four months, remain stuck at aid corridors, along with hundreds of pallets of life-saving nutrition treatments.

3. UN agencies like the World Food Programme (WFP) and UNICEF continue to sound the alarm. [I] "Families in Gaza are starving while food sits at the border," said WFP Executive Director Cindy McCain. [II] "If we wait until famine is declared, it will be too late for many." [III] Both leaders stress that this crisis could have been prevented and call on all parties to allow immediate access for humanitarian aid. [IV]

4. The situation is especially dire for children. Seventeen UN agencies and NGOs confirm that extreme food deprivation is widespread among Gaza's youngest residents. Combined with the collapse of health services and lack of clean water, this has triggered rapid increases in acute malnutrition, particularly in the North Gaza, Gaza, and Rafah governorates. UNICEF warns that its remaining supplies for treating malnutrition are critically low, and WFP has already exhausted its food stocks. All 25 WFP-supported bakeries closed weeks ago, and food parcels and meal support programs have ended.

5. Despite these grim conditions, aid agencies remain ready to act. Both WFP and UNICEF are on the ground, prepared to deliver life-saving assistance as soon as borders reopen. They urge all parties to prioritize the needs of civilians and respect international humanitarian law, stressing that urgent action is the only way to prevent a full-scale famine in Gaza.
questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Gaza's infrastructure has been completely destroyed after the conflict.
Food prices in Gaza can be controlled with proper measures.
Aid agencies are withdrawing from Gaza due to ongoing conflict.
Gaza is on the brink of famine due to conflict and blockade.
questions.explanation: Every paragraph builds the same point: hunger is "expected to exceed famine thresholds", the crisis "is being fueled by ongoing conflict, a complete blockade", and urgent action is needed "to prevent a full-scale famine".

questions.passage:
Being healthy isn't just about eating vegetables or going to the gym. True health includes your body, your mind, and your relationships. For students, understanding health in a (29)____ way can help you manage stress, stay focused, and feel better overall. It's not about being perfect. It's about making choices that support your well-being every day.

Physical health means giving your body what it needs to function well. That includes eating a (30)____ diet, drinking enough water, staying active, and getting 8–10 hours of sleep each night. You don't need to follow strict routines. Just find ways to move your body and rest regularly. Treating your body with care helps you stay energized, concentrate in class, and avoid burnout.

Mental and emotional health is just as important. School can be stressful, and it's normal to feel anxious or down at times. Learning how to manage those emotions, (31)____ by talking to someone, journaling, or simply taking a break, is a key part of staying healthy. If things ever feel too overwhelming, asking for help is not a weakness but a sign of strength.

Finally, social health involves your relationships. Having people you trust and feel safe with can (32)____ a big difference. Healthy communication, respect, and support help you grow emotionally and feel connected.

Being healthy means caring for your whole self: body, mind, and heart, so you can live meaningfully and confidently, both at school, at home, or anywhere else.
questions.explanation: "understanding health in a well-rounded way" = considering all its sides (body, mind, relationships), as the passage goes on to do.

For students, understanding health in a (29)____ way can help you manage stress, stay focused, and feel better overall. It's not about being perfect. It's about making choices that support your well-being every day.

Physical health means giving your body what it needs to function well. That includes eating a (30)____ diet, drinking enough water, staying active, and getting 8–10 hours of sleep each night. You don't need to follow strict routines. Just find ways to move your body and rest regularly. Treating your body with care helps you stay energized, concentrate in class, and avoid burnout.

Mental and emotional health is just as important. School can be stressful, and it's normal to feel anxious or down at times. Learning how to manage those emotions, (31)____ by talking to someone, journaling, or simply taking a break, is a key part of staying healthy. If things ever feel too overwhelming, asking for help is not a weakness but a sign of strength.

Finally, social health involves your relationships. Having people you trust and feel safe with can (32)____ a big difference. Healthy communication, respect, and support help you grow emotionally and feel connected.

Being healthy means caring for your whole self: body, mind, and heart, so you can live meaningfully and confidently, both at school, at home, or anywhere else.
questions.q: What is the most suitable title for the passage?
options: How to perform better at schools
Unhealthy habits to avoid for students
questions.explanation: The passage is addressed to students and covers all three sides of health — physical, mental and social — so "Being healthy as students" fits; diet and school performance are only details.

questions.q: According to the text, what is TRUE about physical health?
options: You have to follow strict exercise routines.
Diet is the most important component.
Being active is not as important as getting rest.
It can help you perform better in class.
questions.explanation: "Treating your body with care helps you stay energized, concentrate in class, and avoid burnout"; the text explicitly says "You don't need to follow strict routines" and ranks no component above the others.

questions.q: What is NOT TRUE about mental health?
options: As students, it's normal to not feel good sometimes.
There are many ways to approach mental self-care.
Strong people do not ask for help.
Managing your emotions is an important part of staying healthy.
questions.explanation: The text says the opposite: "asking for help is not a weakness but a sign of strength"; the other three are stated in paragraph 3.

questions.q: We live in a ______ society where people buy things they don't need just to impress others or feel good about themselves. (CONSUMER)
accept: consumerist
consumer
questions.explanation: An adjective describing a society obsessed with buying: "a consumerist society" ("consumer society" is also a recognised phrase).

questions.q: Ariana Grande's voice is so ______ that you can recognize her singing instantly. (DISTINCT)
accept: distinctive
questions.explanation: "distinctive" = having a quality that makes something easy to recognise — the clue is "you can recognize her singing instantly".

questions.q: Scientists discovered ______ cave paintings that are believed to be over 10,000 years old. (HISTORY)
accept: prehistoric
questions.explanation: Cave paintings over 10,000 years old date from before written history, so the adjective is "prehistoric".

questions.q: My ______ family taught me a lot about Thai customs and cuisine during my exchange program. (HOME)
accept: homestay
questions.explanation: On an exchange program you live with a "homestay family" — the local family that hosts you.

questions.q: She has a ______ fear of failure and it makes her nervous before every exam. (ROOT)
accept: deep-rooted
deeply rooted
deeply-rooted
deep rooted
questions.explanation: A compound adjective before "fear": "a deep-rooted fear" = one that is firmly established and hard to remove.

questions.q: We prefer learning science through ______ experiments rather than through theories. (HAND)
accept: hands-on
hands on
questions.explanation: "hands-on experiments" = practical, doing things yourself — contrasted with "theories".

questions.q: In ______ to free daily guided tours, the museum also offers audio guides for visitors who want to explore by themselves. (ADD)
accept: addition
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase "in addition to" = as well as; the noun form of ADD is needed after "In".

questions.q: Jack is terrified of ______, so he is always busying himself with work. (BORE)
accept: boredom
questions.explanation: A noun is needed after "terrified of": "boredom" — the state of being bored, which he avoids by keeping busy.

questions.q:
It was not wise of you to use the word before checking its definition. (LOOKED)
→ You ______ to using it.
accept: should have looked up its definition prior
should have looked its definition up prior
should have looked up the definition prior
should have looked up the word's definition prior
should have looked up its meaning prior
should have looked the word up prior
should have looked up the word prior
questions.answer: should have looked up its definition prior
questions.explanation: "should have + past participle" criticises a past action, "look up" = check in a dictionary, and "prior to + V-ing" is needed because the sentence ends in "to using it".

questions.q:
No other student studied as hard as the competition winner. (WON)
→ The student ______ hardest.
accept: who won the competition studied the
who won the competition studied
that won the competition studied the
that won the competition studied
questions.answer: who won the competition studied the
questions.explanation: "No other … as hard as X" = X studied (the) hardest; "the competition winner" becomes the relative clause "the student who won the competition".

questions.q:
Sherlock Holmes managed to catch the murderer even with little evidence. (STOP)
→ The lack ______ catching the murderer.
accept: of evidence did not stop Sherlock Holmes from
of evidence didn't stop Sherlock Holmes from
of evidence did not stop Holmes from
of evidence didn't stop Holmes from
of evidence did not stop him from
of evidence didn't stop him from
of evidence could not stop Sherlock Holmes from
of evidence couldn't stop Sherlock Holmes from
questions.answer: of evidence did not stop Sherlock Holmes from
questions.explanation: "stop somebody from + V-ing": the lack of evidence did not stop Sherlock Holmes from catching the murderer.

questions.q:
Our teacher said, "Your critical thinking will improve if you read nonfiction books." (BETTER)
→ Our teacher recommended ______.
accept: reading nonfiction books to better our critical thinking
reading nonfiction books to better your critical thinking
reading nonfiction books to better critical thinking
reading nonfiction books for better critical thinking
reading nonfiction books for our better critical thinking
questions.answer: reading nonfiction books to better our critical thinking
questions.explanation: "recommend + V-ing", and "better" is used as a verb meaning "improve": reading nonfiction books to better our critical thinking.

questions.q:
Jerry was punished by his teacher for bullying his friends. (RECEIVED)
→ Since Jerry ______ from the teacher.
accept: bullied his friends, he received punishment
bullied his friends, he received a punishment
had bullied his friends, he received punishment
had bullied his friends, he received a punishment
was bullying his friends, he received punishment
was bullying his friends, he received a punishment
questions.answer: bullied his friends, he received punishment
questions.explanation: "Since" here means "because": the reason (bullying his friends) comes first, and the passive "was punished" becomes "received (a) punishment from the teacher".

questions.q:
"I'll visit your mother next week, for sure." Sammy said. (PAY)
→ Sammy promised ______ week.
accept: to pay my mother a visit the following
to pay my mother a visit the next
to pay my mother a visit next
to pay a visit to my mother next
questions.answer: to pay my mother a visit the following
questions.explanation: "promise + to-infinitive", "pay somebody a visit" = visit somebody, and in reported speech "next week" becomes "the following week".

questions.q:
I regret revising for the test last minute. (ONLY)
→ ______ earlier.
accept: If only I had revised for the test
If only I'd revised for the test
If only I had revised for it
If only I'd revised for it
questions.answer: If only I had revised for the test
questions.explanation: "If only + past perfect" expresses regret about the past: If only I had revised for the test earlier.
